content: 1. Schools establish both formal and informal partnerships with local community stakeholders, including local government, to support Health-Promoting Schools (HPS) initiatives. 2. The school curriculum is designed to promote health, positive relationships, safety, physical activity, healthy nutrition, and overall well-being. This is achieved through the development of knowledge, skills, attitudes, and behaviors among students, teachers, and the broader school community. 3. Comprehensive school health services, including school nutrition and food provision, are integrated into school policies and aligned with national policies and legal frameworks. 4. School health services are tailored to meet the specific needs and priorities of the school and local community. These services are delivered in a manner that is timely, culturally sensitive, age-appropriate, gender-responsive, rights-based, and evidence-based. 5. Resources, training, and funding are allocated to support school health services, including nutrition and food provision. 6. A system is in place to plan, monitor, and evaluate the progress and performance of school health services. This includes quality assurance and adherence to established standards. 7. Students are actively involved in school governance, including participation in school councils and HPS design teams, alongside parents, caregivers, and local community members. 8. National education policies recognize HPS as a strategy to achieve national development goals through education. These policies provide a framework for the nationwide promotion of HPS. 9. Schools develop policies and plans for regular engagement, communication, and collaboration with stakeholders to support HPS initiatives. 10. School leadership teams, including principals, teachers, administrative staff, school board members, health personnel, students, parents, and caregivers, work collaboratively to promote the values and ethos of HPS. 11. The social-emotional environment within schools is regularly monitored, with actions taken to ensure a positive and supportive atmosphere. 12. Training and professional development opportunities are provided to school staff to enhance their understanding of health literacy and effective teaching strategies that align with the HPS approach. 13. The content and delivery of the school curriculum are regularly reviewed and revised to ensure alignment with health and well-being objectives. 14. Parents, caregivers, and local community representatives are included in school governance structures and HPS design teams to foster collaboration and shared responsibility. 15. A system is established to ensure regular planning and monitoring of school governance and leadership performance in relation to HPS. 16. School health services are adaptable to public health emergencies and emerging needs, ensuring continuity and relevance in service delivery. 17. Global, national, and subnational levels of responsibility are clearly defined for the implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of HPS initiatives. 18. A comprehensive resource bank is available to support the design, planning, and implementation of HPS and related health initiatives, including resources for managing public health crises like COVID-19. 19. Stakeholder engagement is emphasized, with tools and frameworks provided to identify, map, and involve stakeholders effectively in HPS implementation. 20. Evaluation frameworks and guidelines are available to monitor the effectiveness of HPS initiatives, ensuring alignment with global and national standards. 21. Schools are encouraged to use evidence-based practices and resources to address barriers and enablers in implementing HPS, fostering sustainable and impactful health promotion efforts.
